newsitem.title: INDIA: World gold plunge fails to push up Indian demand.
newsitem.headline: World gold plunge fails to push up Indian demand.

text.p: Gold's plunge in world markets to its lowest levels for 12 years had little impact on demand in India, the world's largest importer of the yellow metal, dealers said on Friday.
"We are passing through a lean period. The movement of world prices has had no impact on demand for gold," said M.L. Damani, president of the Bombay Bullion Association.
The low world prices had pushed the prices down on the local bullion market, dealers said.
Standard gold (24 carats) closed 35 rupees lower at 4,365 rupees per 10 grammes, dealers said.
Damani said the marginal gains the rupee had made against the dollar also dampened demand.
He said premiums on special import licences required to import gold had fallen to 9.8 percent from about 13 percent a week ago.
"This indicated a lack of interest in gold imports," Damani said.
The cost of imported gold, inclusive of an import duty of 220 rupees per 10 grammes and taxes, worked out to around 4,340 rupees, which left a very little margin for the importer.
"We are watching the world gold market price situation," Damani said.
Dealers said demand for gold in the three months of June, July and August was always dull because potential buyers in rural areas were busy sowing crops with the onset of the monsoon.
"One can expect some rural demand around September," Damani said. ($=35.77 rupees)
